President of the Fédération Internationale de Football Association, Gianni Infantino, has arrived in Delta State to inspect the renovated Warri City Stadium ahead of its commissioning. Infantino arrived in Osubi, Delta State, where he was received ahead of the inspection of the sporting facility. His arrival was announced in a post on X on Friday by the Executive Assistant on New Media to the Delta State Governor, Dr Samuel Fadele, who wrote, “FIFA President is here in Osubi to inspect the renovated Warri City Stadium.” Speaking in an interview with Arise News, Infantino reaffirmed FIFA’s commitment to making football accessible to everyone, everywhere, stressing the importance of smaller stadiums and grassroots sporting facilities. “Yeah, that’s what football is about, isn’t it? It’s for everyone, everywhere,” he said. He added that football was not limited to big stadiums and the World Cup but also involved smaller facilities that brought the game closer to communities. It’s the proximity, and to be here in Warri for me is a fantastic occasion to showcase what we are about in FIFA, what we are about in football,” he said. Infantino also expressed excitement about his reception in Nigeria, describing his visit as an opportunity to celebrate the country’s passion for football. “Oh yes, I’m feeling so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. This is based, of course, on many years of joint life together, of projects that we’ve put in place, of changing lives of girls and boys,” he said. He said he witnessed the team’s final against Japan, adding that the victory made Nigeria and the African continent proud. Infantino said FIFA would continue working to extend such opportunities to more girls and boys in Nigeria and across Africa.
